Interface TaskRepository

All Superinterfaces:
org.springframework.data.repository.CrudRepository<TaskEntity, Long>, org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository<TaskEntity, Long>, org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaSpecificationExecutor<TaskEntity>, org.springframework.data.repository.ListCrudRepository<TaskEntity, Long>, org.springframework.data.repository.ListPagingAndSortingRepository<TaskEntity, Long>, org.springframework.data.repository.PagingAndSortingRepository<TaskEntity, Long>, org.springframework.data.repository.query.QueryByExampleExecutor<TaskEntity>, org.springframework.data.repository.Repository<TaskEntity, Long>
@Repository public interface TaskRepository extends org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaRepository<TaskEntity, Long>, org.springframework.data.jpa.repository.JpaSpecificationExecutor<TaskEntity>
============================================================================== Task Repository (Data Access Layer) ============================================================================== Manages database persistence, dynamic filtering, and pagination for TaskEntity.

Key Concepts for Beginners:

  • JpaSpecificationExecutor<TaskEntity>: Allows executing dynamic, multi-field filter queries built programmatically with the JPA Criteria API (see TaskServiceImpl#getTasks). For example, searching by status AND keyword search in the title simultaneously.
  • EntityGraph and the N+1 Query Problem: In TaskEntity, the user relationship is marked FetchType.LAZY. If you load 20 tasks and then loop through them calling task.getUser().getUsername(), Hibernate would execute 1 initial query for tasks + 20 separate queries for each user (21 queries in total!). Annotating a query with @EntityGraph(attributePaths = {"user"}) tells Hibernate: "Perform a SQL LEFT JOIN to fetch the tasks and their associated users in ONE single query."
  • Pagination (Pageable and Page<T>): Databases can hold millions of rows. Never load all rows at once into memory. Passing Pageable limits query results via SQL LIMIT and OFFSET, returning a Page that includes the requested slice of data and total count metadata.
